The first assumption we have to make is about perspective. Everything that we are, and our idea of "perceiving" the world, is based on the chemical properties of our bodies, which are governed by physics. Our experience of the world relies on the little engines of our mitochondria firing, our neurons reaching an action potential, and information reaching our senses.

Imagine for a second, just for your body, all that stopped, right down to electrons orbiting nuclei. Say it did this for a week. To the rest of the world, a week passed, but for you, time did not exist. Without the physics happening in your body, no time is experienced for you, you didn't get older, you didn't think, you didn't feel. To you, it's the same as if you traveled through time one week.

Why does this matter? Because according to relativity, there is a universal constant speed limit, and the closer you get to it, the more energy it takes to achieve additional motion. That last part is key; it's not that an object with inertia loses potential energy the faster it gets, it still HAS all that energy, it's just that additional energy isn't producing as much additional momentum.

This matters, because your whole existence is one long chain of chemical reactions, who rely on the momentum of billions of molecules all moving about in that water sack you call a body.

If you start moving on a space ship faster and faster, these processes in your body don't receive more energy, but relativity says, it takes more energy to make things move the same speed when you are already going really fast. That means, everything your body does, now happens slower, just because the same ol' chemical reaction isn't happening as fast as it used to.

However, this doesn't really change the outcome of the reactions , chemical reactions are governed by thresholds being reached. Those thresholds will happen whether it takes the molecules involved 10 nanoseconds or 10 years to get together correctly. As long as the whole process is speeding up or slowing down at the same rate: the end result is the same reactions take place.

So because of this property of movement, the faster your space ship, the longer it will take the molecules on your body to do things, and the slower your perception of time. This is the key, everything around you isn't moving faster, your body is just taking so long to perceive the same old things, and our entire perception of the world is based on our everyday benchmarks like the beating of our own hearts and how long it takes us to "feel" a second, that everything else outside the ship looks faster by comparison.

There thought that this is also why 5 minutes always seems to feel longer to children than adults, our heads are bigger, it takes longer for all the nerve impulses to bounce around and produce a thought, so they experience reality faster :).

So reality itself is not speeding up or slowing down, how we perceive things to happen is, and it's doing so because when you go faster, all the processes happening inside you can't go as fast.
